pages.bodyHtml:
The ASNT NDT Level III visual testing (VT) exam is a 90-question, 2-hour computer-based method exam. You need 70% to pass. Paired with the Level III Basic, it earns an ASNT NDT Level III certificate in VT. It tests the science and control behind visual inspection: the physiology of vision, light and lighting, direct and remote techniques, optical aids, borescopes and video systems, measurement, discontinuities in materials and welds, and the codes and procedures a VT Level III writes and approves. Visual testing is the first method applied to almost every component, and at Level III it is examined as a controlled method with its own variables, not as simply "looking".

Who VT Level III exam prep is for

VT Level III candidates come from three directions. Weld inspectors in fabrication and construction already spend their day on visual acceptance and want the ASNT credential that lets them run the VT part of an employer's written practice. Maintenance and in-service inspectors in refineries, power plants and aerospace use remote visual equipment every day (borescopes, videoscopes, crawler cameras) and need the theory of optics, resolution and lighting behind it. Multi-method Level IIIs add VT because their company's written practice lists VT as a method and needs a Level III for it.

Whatever the background, VT candidates share one advantage and one risk. The advantage is that the method is familiar and the equipment is simple, so study time goes into understanding rather than operation. The risk is overconfidence. Candidates who treat VT as the easy method skip vision science, photometry and optics, which are exactly the areas the exam uses to tell a Level III from an experienced Level II. Our week-one diagnostic is built to show you quickly whether that risk applies to you.

A note on scope: ASNT VT Level III is a personnel certification in the visual testing method under ASNT's programme. It is a different credential from a welding inspector certification issued by a welding society. Some employers ask for both. Atlantis prepares candidates for the ASNT VT Level III exam only.

ASNT Level III VT exam structure

ItemASNT NDT Level III VT method exam
Number of questions90 multiple-choice items
Time allowed2 hours
Passing score70%
FormatComputer-based, scheduled through Pearson VUE
Also required for a first certificateASNT Level III Basic exam
Validity and renewal5 years. Renew by 25 points or by retaking the VT method exam.

Eligibility follows ASNT's three routes: 12 months (252 days) of NDT experience with a four-year engineering or physical science degree, 24 months (504 days) with two years of such study, or 48 months (1,008 days) with no college requirement.

What the VT Level III exam covers

We organise the ASNT VT body of knowledge, which follows the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 visual topical outline at Level III depth, into six domains.

1. Vision and the eye

Anatomy and physiology of the eye, visual acuity and how it is tested, colour vision, contrast sensitivity, fatigue, and the factors that change what an inspector can resolve: angle, distance, glare, adaptation. Candidates are sometimes surprised by how much of the exam sits here. It underpins why codes specify viewing distance, angle and lighting.

2. Light and lighting

Photometric units (illuminance in lux and foot-candles, luminance), the inverse square law for light, colour temperature and rendering, reflection, glare, shadowing and oblique lighting to reveal surface texture. You should know the minimum illumination and viewing geometry for direct visual examination required by ASME Section V Article 9 and how compliance is measured with a light meter.

3. Direct and remote visual techniques

Direct visual examination with and without optical aids (magnifiers, mirrors), and remote visual examination with rigid borescopes, fiberscopes, videoscopes, pan-tilt-zoom cameras and robotic crawlers. Optics fundamentals appear here: magnification, field of view, depth of field, resolution, and how each is traded off in a remote system. A Level III must demonstrate that a remote system resolves at least what the procedure requires, usually with a resolution target.

4. Measurement and documentation

Weld gauges, fillet gauges, calipers, micrometers, depth gauges, pit gauges, comparators, and measurement on video systems (stereo, shadow and phase measurement). Also documentation: photography, video recording, replication, and what makes a visual record acceptable as evidence.

5. Materials, processes and discontinuities

Discontinuities from casting, forging, rolling, machining and welding, and service damage such as corrosion, erosion, fatigue cracking, wear and deformation. Weld discontinuities get particular attention: cracks, porosity, undercut, overlap, incomplete fusion and penetration, excess reinforcement, misalignment and arc strikes, and how weld profile is evaluated.

6. Codes, standards and procedures

ASME Section V Article 9 for visual examination, construction-code acceptance criteria (the AWS D1.1 visual inspection criteria, ASME B31.3 and API 1104 as common examples), procedure content and demonstration of the procedure where the code requires it.

A 6-week VT Level III study plan

WeekFocusOutput
1Diagnostic; the eye, acuity, colour vision, visual perceptionGap map
2Light and lighting: units, inverse square law, glare, oblique lighting; ASME V Article 9 requirementsLighting calculation drills
3Optics and remote VT: borescopes, fiberscopes, videoscopes, resolution targetsRemote-system scenario set
4Measurement tools and documentation; first timed 45-question setTimed score
5Material and weld discontinuities; AWS D1.1, B31.3 and API 1104 acceptance logic; procedure contentDraft VT procedure outline reviewed
6Full 90-question timed mock, error-log review, second mockGo / no-go decision

Key references for the VT Level III exam

  • ASNT Nondestructive Testing Handbook, Visual Testing volume.
  • ASNT Level III Study Guide: Visual Testing.
  • ASNT Question & Answer Book for VT.
  • ANSI/ASNT CP-105 VT topical outline.
  • ASME BPVC Section V, Article 9.
  • AWS D1.1 visual inspection acceptance criteria, and AWS B1.11, the guide for the visual examination of welds.
  • ASME B31.3 and API 1104 visual requirements, as common acceptance-criteria examples.

Where experienced VT inspectors lose marks

  • Vision science. Weld inspectors know acceptance criteria but rarely study the eye. Acuity, colour perception and adaptation questions are often the weakest area on a diagnostic.
  • Photometry. Converting between foot-candles and lux, applying the inverse square law to a lamp, and knowing when a light meter reading is valid all come up.
  • Remote optics trade-offs. Larger field of view means less resolution, and more magnification means less depth of field. Questions test whether you can reason through a camera choice, not just name equipment.
  • Procedure demonstration. Knowing when a code requires a procedure to be demonstrated, and how resolution is proven with a target, is typical Level III content.
  • Service damage. Candidates from new construction are strong on weld discontinuities but less sure on corrosion, erosion and fatigue appearance in service.

Two worked examples of VT Level III reasoning

Lighting a direct visual examination. A procedure calls for direct visual examination of a fillet weld inside a vessel nozzle. The Level III has to confirm three things: that the inspector's eye can get within the viewing distance and angle the code requires, that the illumination at the surface meets the code minimum when measured with a calibrated light meter at the surface being examined, and that glare from a shiny weld cap or shadows from the nozzle wall do not hide surface features. If the eye cannot reach the required distance or angle, the examination is no longer direct. It becomes remote, and the procedure must then show that the remote system provides resolution at least equivalent to direct viewing. The exam frames these as short scenarios: a light reading at one distance, a lamp moved to another, and the question of whether the examination is still compliant. The inverse square law answers most of them.

Choosing a remote system for a boiler header. Access is through a small inspection port, the header is dark and several metres long, and the concern is ligament cracking between tube holes. A rigid borescope gives excellent image quality but cannot turn corners. A fiberscope bends but its fibre bundle limits resolution. A videoscope with articulation, a suitable light source and measurement capability is usually the answer, but the Level III still has to prove resolution at the working distance with a target, set the lighting to avoid washout on bright surfaces, and specify how images are recorded so a finding can be reviewed later. Questions on this topic test the trade-offs, not the brand names.

What a VT Level III does day to day

In a fabrication business, the VT Level III approves the visual procedure, sets lighting and viewing requirements, qualifies inspectors' measurement technique, and resolves disputes over weld profile and acceptance. In maintenance and in-service programmes, the Level III selects remote visual equipment for confined or hazardous access, proves system resolution, defines how findings are recorded, and ties visual results to follow-up by other methods. In every setting, the Level III writes and grades the VT Level I and II examinations under the employer's written practice and signs off training records. VT findings often decide which other methods are applied next, so the VT Level III is also frequently the person who writes the inspection plan. The exam's mix of vision science, optics, discontinuities and code logic reflects that breadth.

How Atlantis VT Level III exam prep works

The course is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, in live online sessions, recorded for shift workers.

  • Vision and lighting sessions covering the science most weld inspectors have never been taught formally.
  • Remote VT sessions on optics trade-offs, resolution targets and measurement on video systems.
  • Timed practice questions in the 90-question, 2-hour format with explanations, and two full mocks.
  • Procedure review of a VT procedure outline against ASME Section V Article 9 and your governing construction code.
  • Practical NDT scenarios: the Practical NDT simulator, the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal, includes visual inspection scenarios in environments such as a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace real inspection experience.

Request a VT Level III prep schedule, or warm up with our free VT Level II practice questions.

Employer sponsorship for VT Level III candidates

Visual testing is on almost every written practice, and a VT Level III is often the easiest additional method for an existing Level III to add. It closes an audit gap quickly. The ASNT certificate is the credential. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer still certifies its Level III under its own written practice. We support both sides, including a written practice review. Ask about a private VT Level III cohort or use the training enquiry form.

ASNT Level III VT exam: frequently asked questions

How many questions are on the ASNT Level III VT exam?

90 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours, per ASNT's Level III examination listing.

What is the passing score?

70%.

Is ASNT VT Level III the same as a welding inspector certification?

No. ASNT VT Level III certifies you in the visual testing method under ASNT's programme. Welding inspector certifications are separate credentials from other bodies. Atlantis prepares candidates for the ASNT exam only.

Does the exam include remote visual inspection?

Yes. Borescopes, fiberscopes, videoscopes, cameras and crawlers, and the optics behind them, are all in the body of knowledge.

Are there calculations on the VT exam?

A few, mostly lighting (inverse square law, unit conversion) and optics (magnification, field of view) questions.

How long should I study?

About 6 weeks at 6 to 8 hours a week after the Basic. Weld inspectors usually spend extra time on vision science and remote optics.

Can VT be my first Level III method?

Yes. Basic plus the VT method exam gives an ASNT NDT Level III certificate in VT.

How is a VT Level III certificate renewed?

Every five years, by 25 renewal points or by retaking the VT method exam.

Can VT Level III preparation be done online?

Yes. The exam is written and computer-based, and our preparation runs live online.

How do we get a quote for several candidates?

Send candidate numbers and target dates. We quote within one business day.

pages.bodyHtml:
The ASNT NDT Level III electromagnetic testing (ET) exam is a 135-question, 4-hour computer-based method exam. You need 70% to pass. Together with the Level III Basic, it earns an ASNT NDT Level III certificate in electromagnetic testing. Eddy current testing is the core of the method. The exam tests electromagnetic induction, the impedance plane, conductivity, permeability and standard depth of penetration, probe and coil design, frequency selection and multifrequency mixing, tubing, surface, conductivity and coating-thickness applications, and the codes and procedures an ET Level III approves. With UT and RT, it is one of the three longest Level III method exams, and it is the most abstract of them.

Who ET Level III exam prep is for

ET Level III candidates are a smaller, more specialised group than UT or RT candidates, and they usually come from one of three backgrounds. Tubing specialists inspect heat exchanger, condenser and boiler tubes with bobbin probes in refineries, chemical plants and power stations, and are expert at reading Lissajous signals from supports, dents and wall loss. Aerospace technicians use surface probes and bolt-hole probes for crack detection around fasteners and on wheels, and run conductivity checks to verify heat treatment. Manufacturing technicians run encircling-coil systems on bar, tube and wire lines, or sort materials by conductivity and hardness.

Each group knows its own application deeply and the others hardly at all. The Level III exam spans all of them and goes underneath them into the physics. A tubing analyst who has never set up a surface-crack test, or an aerospace technician who has never seen a bobbin signal, needs a structured plan to cover the unfamiliar half.

ItemASNT NDT Level III ET method exam
Number of questions135 multiple-choice items
Time allowed4 hours
Passing score70%
FormatComputer-based, scheduled through Pearson VUE
Also required for a first certificateASNT Level III Basic exam
Validity and renewal5 years. Renew by 25 points or by retaking the ET method exam.

ASNT's eligibility routes are the same for every Level III method: 12 months (252 days) of NDT experience with a four-year engineering or physical science degree, 24 months (504 days) with two years of such study, or 48 months (1,008 days) with no college requirement.

What the ET Level III exam covers

We organise ASNT's electromagnetic testing body of knowledge, which follows the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outline at Level III depth, into six domains. Eddy current carries most of the weight. Related electromagnetic techniques, such as remote field testing and alternating current field measurement, can also appear, so we cover their principles.

1. Electromagnetic principles

Faraday's law of induction, Lenz's law, magnetic fields around a coil, self and mutual inductance, inductive reactance, resistance and impedance, and phase. You should be comfortable with how coil impedance changes when a conductor enters the field, and why.

2. Material properties and depth of penetration

Electrical conductivity (and the %IACS scale), magnetic permeability, and the standard depth of penetration, which falls as frequency, conductivity or permeability rise. Expect calculation questions and questions on the phase lag with depth that lets an analyst estimate how deep a flaw lies. Ferromagnetic materials get special attention: why permeability variations swamp flaw signals, and how magnetic saturation or other techniques address that.

3. The impedance plane and signal analysis

The normalised impedance plane, lift-off and fill-factor effects, the conductivity curve, the characteristic frequency, and the direction and phase of signals from cracks, wall loss, dents, deposits, support plates and conductivity changes. Signal analysis questions often show a signal and ask what it represents or which variable produced it.

4. Probes, coils and instrumentation

Surface (pancake and pencil) probes, encircling coils, internal bobbin probes, absolute and differential configurations, bridge and reflection (driver-pickup) arrangements, shielding and focusing, array probes, and rotating probes. Instrument settings: frequency, gain, phase rotation, filtering (high-pass and low-pass), and display modes.

5. Techniques and applications

Frequency selection for a given depth and material, multifrequency operation and mixing to suppress support-plate or other unwanted signals, calibration and reference standards (flat-bottom holes, through-wall holes, EDM notches, conductivity standards), tubing inspection and sizing, surface-crack detection, bolt-hole inspection, conductivity measurement, coating-thickness measurement, and sorting.

6. Codes, standards and procedures

ASME Section V Article 8 for eddy current examination of tubular products, the relevant ASTM practices, procedure content and essential variables, and the reporting of results.

A 12-week ET Level III study plan

WeekFocusOutput
1Diagnostic; induction, Lenz's law, inductance, reactance and impedanceGap map; formula sheet started
2Conductivity, %IACS, permeability; depth of penetration and phase lagDepth-of-penetration drills
3The normalised impedance plane; lift-off, fill factor, characteristic frequencyImpedance-plane question set
4Probes and coils: surface, encircling, bobbin; absolute and differential; driver-pickupProbe-selection drills
5Instrumentation, filtering, phase rotation, displaysSettings scenario set
6Tubing inspection: calibration standards, signal analysis, sizing; first timed setTimed 45-question score
7Multifrequency mixing; ferromagnetic tubing, saturation, remote field principlesMixing concept set
8Surface and bolt-hole crack detection; array and rotating probesSurface application set
9Conductivity, coating thickness, sorting; other electromagnetic techniquesApplications set
10ASME V Article 8, ASTM practices, procedure contentDraft ET procedure outline reviewed
11Full 135-question timed mock; error logMock score
12Error-log review, second mock, logisticsGo / no-go decision

Key references for the ET Level III exam

  • ASNT Nondestructive Testing Handbook, Electromagnetic Testing volume.
  • ASNT Level III Study Guide: Electromagnetic Testing.
  • ASNT Question & Answer Book for ET.
  • ANSI/ASNT CP-105 electromagnetic testing topical outline.
  • ASME BPVC Section V, Article 8 (eddy current examination of tubular products).
  • ASTM E243 (copper and copper-alloy tubes), E426 (stainless and similar alloy tubular products), E309 (steel tubular products using magnetic saturation).
  • ASTM E1004 (electrical conductivity), E376 (coating thickness), E2096 (remote field testing of ferromagnetic tubes) and E2261 (alternating current field measurement of welds).

Where experienced ET technicians lose marks

  • Physics without an instrument. Analysts who read signals expertly on a screen often cannot explain why a signal rotates the way it does. The exam asks why.
  • Depth of penetration direction. Raising frequency reduces penetration, and so do higher conductivity and permeability. Under time pressure candidates reverse one of the three.
  • Absolute versus differential. Knowing which configuration responds to gradual changes and which to abrupt ones, and what each does with long, uniform wall loss, is standard content.
  • Mixing. Why two frequencies are needed to cancel a support-plate signal, and what the mix does to other signals, is often the weakest topic on a diagnostic.
  • The other half of the method. Tubing specialists lose marks on surface, conductivity and coating questions. Aerospace technicians lose them on bobbin analysis and tube standards.

Choosing a test frequency: a worked example of Level III reasoning

Frequency selection is the decision ET questions return to most often, because it links the physics to the result. Take a non-ferromagnetic heat exchanger tube where the concern is wall loss starting from the outside surface. Too high a frequency concentrates the eddy currents near the inside surface, so outside-diameter defects give weak signals with poor phase separation. Too low a frequency gives deep penetration but poor sensitivity and poor phase discrimination between defect depths. The usual reasoning sets the primary frequency so the phase separation between inside and outside surface indications on the reference standard falls in a useful range, then adds a lower frequency that responds strongly to support plates so the two can be mixed and the support signal suppressed. A higher frequency may be added for inside-surface conditions.

Switch the problem to a surface crack in an aluminium aircraft skin and the logic changes. Now high frequency is an advantage, because the currents crowd at the surface where the crack is and lift-off can be separated by phase. For a crack in a second layer under a fastener, the Level III goes the other way again and chooses a low frequency to reach the subsurface layer, accepting reduced resolution. The exam asks versions of all three problems. Candidates who understand why the choice changes do far better than those who have memorised a single application.

Other electromagnetic techniques: what a Level III should know

Ferromagnetic tubing defeats conventional eddy current because permeability variations swamp flaw signals. Two answers come up. Magnetic saturation uses a strong DC field to push permeability down so conventional eddy current works. Remote field testing uses a low-frequency exciter and a detector spaced well apart, so the field passes through the tube wall twice, giving through-wall sensitivity in carbon steel tubing without saturation. Alternating current field measurement induces a uniform current in a surface and measures field disturbances around surface-breaking cracks, often through coatings, which makes it useful for weld toe inspection on structures. Magnetic flux leakage, which ASNT now lists as its own Level III method, detects field leakage from wall loss in magnetised steel. Knowing when each technique fits, and what limits it, is enough for most exam questions on them.

What an ET Level III does day to day

In a tubing programme, the ET Level III writes the technique and calibration requirements, approves the analysis guidelines that tell analysts how to call and size indications, resolves disputed calls, and reports tube condition to the plant engineer. In aerospace and manufacturing, the Level III develops techniques for specific parts and cracks, designs or approves reference standards, and validates conductivity and coating measurements. In every setting, the Level III writes and grades the company's ET Level I and II examinations under the written practice. The weight the exam puts on physics, signals and procedures matches that work.

How Atlantis ET Level III exam prep works

The course is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, in live online sessions, recorded for shift and outage workers.

  • Impedance-plane workshops that build the plane from first principles, so signal questions become reasoning rather than memory.
  • Cross-application sessions that take tubing specialists through surface work and surface specialists through tubing.
  • Timed practice questions with explanations, and two full 135-question mocks.
  • Procedure review of an ET procedure outline against ASME Section V Article 8 and the relevant ASTM practice.
  • Method refresh on Practical NDT: the Practical NDT simulator, the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal, includes eddy current scenarios across its 12 methods and 5 virtual environments. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on work.

Request an ET Level III prep schedule, or warm up with our free ET Level II practice questions.

Employer sponsorship for ET Level III candidates

ET Level IIIs are scarce, and outage schedules do not wait for an outside Level III's availability. Companies that run tube inspection or aerospace eddy current work often sponsor a senior analyst so that analysis guidelines, calibration standards and examinations are controlled in-house. The ASNT certificate is the credential. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer still certifies its Level III under its written practice. We support both the candidate and the company's written practice. Ask about a private ET Level III cohort or use the training enquiry form.

ASNT Level III ET exam: frequently asked questions

How many questions are on the ASNT Level III ET exam?

135 multiple-choice questions in 4 hours, per ASNT's Level III examination listing.

What is the passing score?

70%.

Is the ET exam only about eddy current?

Eddy current is the core. ASNT's electromagnetic testing method is broader, so principles of related techniques such as remote field testing and alternating current field measurement can also appear.

Are there calculations on the ET exam?

Yes. Expect depth of penetration, inductive reactance and impedance, fill factor and conductivity questions.

I only do tube inspection. Is that enough?

Usually not. The exam covers surface, bolt-hole, conductivity and coating applications too. Our plan fills whichever side you have not worked.

How long should I study for ET Level III?

We plan 12 weeks at 6 to 8 hours a week. It is the most abstract method exam, so candidates rarely compress the physics weeks.

Do I need the Basic too?

Yes. A first ASNT NDT Level III certificate needs the Basic plus at least one method exam.

How is an ET Level III certificate renewed?

Every five years, by 25 renewal points or by retaking the ET method exam.

Can I prepare for ET Level III online?

Yes. The exam is written and computer-based, and our preparation runs live online, with the Practical NDT simulator available for method refresh.

Can we book a private cohort?

Yes. Send candidate numbers and your outage calendar, and we will quote a schedule that works around it.

pages.bodyHtml:
The ASNT NDT Level II is ASNT's own central certification for Level II technicians in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT, and it meets Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A. Candidates pass a 50-question, 2-hour General exam and at least one 40-question, 2-hour Specific exam in the General Industry or Pressure Equipment sector. The employer still carries out the vision, practical and any job-specific exams its written practice requires. The certificate renews every five years. ASNT's older ACCP programme stopped taking new applications in May 2023 and was replaced by ASNT 9712, a separate scheme built to ISO 9712:2021. Atlantis prepares candidates for the SNT-TC-1A-based ASNT NDT Level II exams.

Three ASNT Level II credentials, and which one this page covers

Searches for "ASNT Level 2 certification" now return three different things, and technicians regularly pay for the wrong one. Here is how they differ, based on ASNT's own programme pages.

CredentialBuilt toStatusWho administers the practical
ASNT NDT Level IIMeets ASNT Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1ACurrent. Methods MT, PT, RT, UT, VT.The employer, under its written practice
ASNT 9712 Level IIISO 9712:2021 and ANSI/ASNT CP-9712Current. Launched March 2023 and replaced ACCP.ASNT authorised exam centres, one practical per technique
ACCP Level IIASNT Central Certification ProgramClosed. No new applications after 15 May 2023, no renewals after 30 August 2023, full sunset by September 2028. Existing certificates run to their expiry.(historic)

This page covers ASNT NDT Level II, the SNT-TC-1A-aligned credential. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, so we do not offer ISO 9712 or ASNT 9712 preparation or practical examinations. If an employer or client specifically requires ASNT 9712, book it through ASNT and its authorised exam centres. The method knowledge on this page still applies, because both schemes test the same physics.

ASNT NDT Level II exam structure

ExamQuestionsTimeContent
General (one per method)50 multiple-choice2 hoursFundamentals, principles and theory from the Level II topical outline for the method in ANSI/ASNT CP-105
Specific (at least one)40 multiple-choice2 hoursBased on an NDT procedure: equipment, operating processes and techniques used in the chosen sector (General Industry or Pressure Equipment)
Vision, practical, job-specificSet by the employer—Carried out by the employer under its written practice

The written exams are computer-based and scheduled through a MyCert account at Pearson VUE or an authorised exam centre. There is no walk-in testing, and you need two valid forms of identification on the day. ASNT's exam page states the question counts and times above. Check it for the current passing requirement and candidate rules when you schedule.

Eligibility: training and experience by method

ASNT publishes minimum training and work experience for the ASNT NDT Level II, stated in days. "Total NDT" means experience across NDT generally, of which the "in method" figure must be in the method you are certifying.

MethodTrainingExperience in methodTotal NDT experience
Magnetic particle (MT)3 days40 days76 days
Liquid penetrant (PT)2 days30 days58 days
Radiographic (RT)12 days120 days229 days
Ultrasonic (UT)12 days120 days229 days
Visual (VT)4 days30 days58 days

These are ASNT's figures for its central Level II. Your employer's written practice may set higher numbers, and the SNT-TC-1A tables your employer uses are expressed differently. See our training requirements matrix for the employer-side view. For the ASNT 9712 Level II, ASNT publishes different figures: 5 days of training for MT, PT and VT, 15 for RT (plus radiation safety) and 18 for UT, with 60 days of experience for MT, PT and VT and 180 for RT and UT.

Who ASNT NDT Level II exam prep is for

Technicians who want a portable credential. Under SNT-TC-1A alone, certification belongs to the employer and ends when you leave. A central ASNT certificate travels with you. Many Level IIs sit the ASNT NDT Level II to show a new employer independent evidence of their knowledge, even though the new employer still certifies them under its own written practice.

Employers that want independent verification. Some inspection companies use the ASNT NDT Level II General and Specific exams in place of, or alongside, in-house written exams, then complete the practical and vision exams themselves. It gives clients and auditors an external benchmark.

Former ACCP holders. ACCP certificates can no longer be renewed through ACCP. Holders are choosing between ASNT NDT Level II and ASNT 9712, depending on what their clients and codes require. If your work is under US codes and SNT-TC-1A written practices, the ASNT NDT Level II is usually the natural fit. We will talk it through with you honestly before you enrol.

What the General and Specific exams test

General exam (per method)

The General exam follows the CP-105 Level II topical outline for the method. For UT that means wave physics, transducers, calibration, straight- and angle-beam techniques and interpretation. For RT it covers radiation physics, exposure, film and digital recording, image quality and safety. For MT it covers magnetism, currents, techniques, particles and demagnetisation. For PT it covers penetrant materials, process steps and interpretation. For VT it covers vision, lighting, optical aids, remote visual equipment and discontinuities. Fifty questions in two hours gives you plenty of time. The difficulty is breadth, especially for technicians who learned one application on the job.

Specific exam (per sector)

The Specific exam is built around an NDT procedure. You are tested on applying a procedure to the equipment and techniques of the General Industry or Pressure Equipment sector: setting up, calibrating, performing the examination and recording results as the procedure requires. The skill being tested is reading a procedure precisely and doing exactly what it says. Technicians who work from habit rather than from the document lose marks here.

How the ASNT NDT Level II fits your employer's SNT-TC-1A programme

The most common misunderstanding about the ASNT NDT Level II is that it replaces the employer's certification. It does not. It supplies the written part of the evidence, independently. A typical sequence for an employer using the credential looks like this:

  1. The employer's written practice is updated to say that the ASNT NDT Level II General and Specific exams will be accepted as the written general and specific examinations for the methods concerned.
  2. The technician completes the formal training hours the written practice requires, often at least ASNT's published minimum for the method, and documents them.
  3. The technician accumulates and documents the required experience in the method.
  4. The technician passes the ASNT General and Specific exams at a test centre.
  5. The employer's Level III administers the vision examination and the practical examination on real specimens, plus any job-specific exam.
  6. The employer certifies the technician as Level II under its written practice, referencing the ASNT certificate in the personnel file.

Done this way, the employer's audit file carries both an external credential and the employer-controlled elements that SNT-TC-1A expects. If your written practice does not yet mention the ASNT exams, a Level III needs to amend it before the credential can count. Atlantis can do that as part of a written practice review.

Where Level II candidates lose marks

  • Breadth outside their application. A pipeline UT technician may never have done straight-beam forging work. A field MT technician may never have used a wet bench. The General exam covers the whole Level II outline.
  • Reading the procedure literally. The Specific exam rewards doing what the procedure says, not what you usually do on site.
  • Formulas. UT and RT candidates who rely on instrument calculations lose easy marks on Snell's law, near field, inverse square and exposure questions.
  • Terminology. Indication, discontinuity and defect have different meanings. Relevant and non-relevant indications are defined terms. Loose field usage costs marks.

An 8-week study plan for one method

WeekFocus
1Diagnostic against the CP-105 Level II outline; read SNT-TC-1A's Level II sections
2–3Principles and theory of the method; formula practice (UT, RT)
4Equipment, calibration and reference standards
5Techniques and interpretation; first timed 50-question General mock
6Procedure reading: working through a sector-style procedure line by line
7Timed 40-question Specific mock; error log
8Second General and Specific mocks; go / no-go decision

MT, PT and VT candidates with good field experience often need 4 to 6 weeks. UT and RT candidates usually need the full 8.

Key references

  • ANSI/ASNT CP-105, the Level II topical outline for your method.
  • ASNT SNT-TC-1A, current edition.
  • ASNT Level II study guides and Question & Answer books for your method.
  • ASNT Nondestructive Testing Handbook volume for your method, used selectively.
  • ASME BPVC Section V (Article 4 UT, Article 2 RT, Article 7 MT, Article 6 PT, Article 9 VT), especially for the Pressure Equipment Specific exam.

How Atlantis ASNT NDT Level II exam prep works

Preparation is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and runs live online, so you can study from a job site or from home.

  • Live online sessions on the CP-105 outline for your method, recorded for shift workers.
  • Timed practice exams built to the 50-question General and 40-question Specific format, with explanations.
  • Procedure-reading drills for the Specific exam.
  • Practical refresh on the Practical NDT simulator. Practical NDT, the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal, lets you practise 12 methods in 5 virtual environments before your employer's practical exam. It is practice only. Your practical must still be performed on real specimens under your employer's written practice.
  • Employer practical support. For companies, Atlantis can deliver the hands-on training and administer the practical examination onsite at your facility, under an ASNT Level III, as part of your SNT-TC-1A programme.

Method-specific Level II training pages: UT Level 2, RT Level 2, MT Level 2, PT Level 2, VT Level 2. Free practice questions: UT Level II practice questions. Request an ASNT NDT Level II prep schedule.

Employer sponsorship

For an employer, sponsoring technicians through the ASNT NDT Level II General and Specific exams gives the written practice an external benchmark and gives clients a credential they recognise. The employer still controls the practical, vision and job-specific exams and issues the SNT-TC-1A certification. Atlantis can cover the full chain: online exam preparation, onsite practical training and examination under a Level III, and a written practice that references the ASNT exams correctly. Ask for a cohort quote or use the training enquiry form.

ASNT NDT Level II exam: frequently asked questions

Is ACCP still available?

No. ASNT stopped accepting new ACCP applications on 15 May 2023 and stopped renewals on 30 August 2023. ASNT 9712 replaced it, and the ACCP programme sunsets fully by September 2028.

What is the difference between ASNT NDT Level II and ASNT 9712 Level II?

ASNT NDT Level II meets SNT-TC-1A, and the employer performs the practical and vision exams. ASNT 9712 is built to ISO 9712:2021, requires practical exams at ASNT authorised exam centres, and has its own training and experience minimums.

How many questions are on the ASNT NDT Level II exams?

The General exam has 50 questions in 2 hours. Each Specific exam has 40 questions in 2 hours.

Which methods are offered?

Magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, radiographic, ultrasonic and visual testing.

Which sectors do the Specific exams cover?

General Industry and Pressure Equipment.

Who gives the practical exam?

For the ASNT NDT Level II, your employer carries out the visual acuity, practical and any job-specific exams required by its written practice.

How long is the certificate valid?

ASNT NDT Level II certificates are renewed every five years.

Does passing make me certified to work?

You still need your employer's certification under its written practice. The ASNT certificate is portable evidence of knowledge. Authorisation to perform and sign inspections comes from the employer.

Does Atlantis prepare candidates for ASNT 9712?

No. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and prepares candidates for the ASNT NDT Level II exams.

Can I prepare online?

Yes. The written exams are computer-based and our preparation runs live online. The practical is completed on real specimens with your employer, or with Atlantis onsite at your facility.

pages.breadcrumb: Can You Get NDT Certified Online?
pages.courseName: Online NDT theory training with onsite practical (ASNT SNT-TC-1A)

pages.subject: Online%20NDT%20certification%20question
pages.bodyHtml:
Partly. You can complete NDT theory training and exam preparation online, but you cannot become fully NDT certified online. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the recommended practice most US employers follow, certification is issued by your employer. It requires documented classroom training, on-the-job experience hours, a vision test, and written general and specific exams plus a hands-on practical exam on real specimens, administered under the employer's written practice. An online course can cover the training hours and prepare you for the written exams. It cannot supply the experience or the practical.

Why "NDT certified online" is a misleading promise

Search for "NDT certification online" and you will find courses that promise a certificate at the end. Read the small print. What they issue is a certificate of training completion: evidence that you attended a number of classroom hours in a method. That is useful, and it counts toward certification, but it is not certification.

In the US, SNT-TC-1A puts certification in the hands of the employer. Each employer writes a written practice, a document that sets its own requirements within the framework of SNT-TC-1A, and certifies its own personnel against it. The employer's Level III (in-house or outsourced) administers the examinations, and the employer signs the certification. When you change employers, your new employer certifies you again under its own written practice, although it can take your training and experience records into account.

Nothing in that process can be completed by a website on its own. The experience hours are spent doing supervised NDT work. The practical exam is performed with real equipment on real specimens, observed and graded under the employer's programme. A course that tells you otherwise is either selling a training certificate under a bigger name, or selling a certification no serious employer will accept.

What you can do online, and what you cannot

Certification step under SNT-TC-1AOnline?Notes
Classroom (formal) training hoursYesLive online and self-paced theory are widely accepted if the employer's written practice allows them and the hours are documented.
Preparation for the general and specific written examsYesPractice questions, mock exams and code-reading drills work well online.
Practice with equipment behaviourPartlySimulation helps you practise technique and interpretation, but it does not replace hands-on time.
On-the-job experience hoursNoPerformed under supervision on real work and documented by the employer.
Vision (eye) examinationNoNear-vision acuity and colour contrast, done in person, typically every year.
Practical examinationNoPerformed on real specimens with real equipment, graded under the written practice.
CertificationNoIssued and signed by the employer.

The training-hour and experience figures behind each method and level are set out in our NDT training requirements matrix. Your employer's written practice may require more than the SNT-TC-1A minimums, never less.

What about ASNT's own certifications?

ASNT also runs central certification programmes, where ASNT, not your employer, issues the certificate. Even these are not fully online:

  • ASNT NDT Level II (meets SNT-TC-1A): computer-based General and Specific exams taken at a Pearson VUE or authorised test centre. The employer still performs the vision, practical and any job-specific exams. See our ASNT NDT Level II exam prep page.
  • ASNT NDT Level III: a Basic exam plus at least one method exam, all computer-based and taken at a test centre, after meeting ASNT's education and experience requirements. See Level III Basic exam prep.
  • ASNT 9712 (built to ISO 9712, replaced ACCP): includes practical exams at ASNT authorised exam centres.

In every case the preparation can be online. The proctored exams, the experience and the practical cannot.

How long does it take?

The online part is the fast part. Level I and II theory for a surface method such as MT or PT can be finished in days. UT and RT theory takes longer, spread over a few weeks for someone who is also working. The experience hours set the real calendar. For UT and RT they are measured in months of supervised work, which is why employers, not individuals, usually drive certification. A trainee is hired, trained, gains experience on the job, and is examined and certified by the employer. Our guide to becoming an NDT technician walks through the sequence.

How Atlantis does it: online theory, onsite practical

Atlantis NDT is built around the honest version of online NDT training. It works because we split the process at exactly the line the table above draws.

  1. Live online theory. Level I and II theory for UT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, taught live online by an ASNT Level III, with recorded replays. The hours are documented so they can be counted under your employer's written practice. See online NDT training.
  2. Practice on the Practical NDT simulator. Between sessions, trainees practise on Practical NDT, the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal: 12 methods in 5 virtual environments (an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank). It builds familiarity with setup, scanning and interpretation before trainees touch real equipment. It is practice. It does not replace the practical exam.
  3. Onsite practical training and examination at the employer's facility. The hands-on part is delivered where the work happens, on the employer's equipment and specimens, under an ASNT Level III, and the practical exam is administered and graded to the written practice. Atlantis has no public classroom, so the practical comes to you.
  4. Written exams and Level III administration. We prepare and grade general and specific exams to the employer's written practice, or support the employer's own Level III in doing so.
  5. Written practice support. If the employer does not yet have a compliant written practice, we can develop or review one, because without it there is nothing to certify against.

For technicians aiming higher, our Level III programme runs fully online, because the ASNT Level III exams are written. The method pages cover each exam: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET.

Want to see how it would work for you or your crew? Ask how online theory and onsite practical fit your situation.

A realistic route: from online theory to certified Level II

Here is how the process usually runs for a new UT technician hired by an inspection company that uses online theory. In the first weeks, the trainee completes Level I theory live online, practises calibration and scanning on the simulator, and starts supervised work alongside a certified Level II, logging experience from day one. The employer's Level III, in-house or outsourced, runs the Level I written exams and a practical on real calibration blocks and weld specimens, and the employer certifies the trainee as Level I. The technician then works as a Level I, performing examinations to procedures under Level II guidance, while completing Level II theory online in evenings or between jobs. Once the Level II experience total in the written practice is reached, the Level II general, specific and practical exams follow, and the employer certifies the technician as Level II.

Online delivery shortened the classroom part and removed the travel. It did not shorten the experience, and it did not move the practical off the shop floor. Any plan that promises otherwise should make you cautious.

How to judge an online NDT course before paying

  • Does it say "certification" or "certificate of training"? An honest provider is precise about which one it issues.
  • Who teaches it? Look for an ASNT Level III in the method, named on the page.
  • Are the hours documented per method and level, in a form your employer's written practice can accept?
  • How is the practical handled? If the answer is "it isn't", you will be paying again later.
  • Does it build to SNT-TC-1A and CP-105 topical outlines, the framework US employers use?
  • Is it live or recorded only? Recorded courses suit refreshers. Live sessions suit first-time learners who need questions answered.

Our article on online versus in-person NDT training goes further into the trade-offs, and what an NDT school can and cannot do covers the institutional side.

If you are an employer

Online theory changes the economics of certifying a crew. Technicians keep working while they complete the classroom hours from a site office, and the practical is run onsite in a concentrated block on your own equipment. Your written practice needs to allow online formal training and describe how the hours are recorded. We can check that for you. Online NDT certification: frequently asked questions

Can you get NDT certified completely online?

No. Theory training and exam preparation can be online, but SNT-TC-1A certification requires on-the-job experience, a vision test and a practical exam on real specimens, and it is issued by your employer.

Is online NDT training accepted by employers?

Generally yes, as formal training hours, provided the employer's written practice allows it and the hours are documented per method and level. Check with the employer before you enrol.

What is the difference between a training certificate and NDT certification?

A training certificate proves you completed classroom hours. Certification is the employer's written confirmation, under its written practice, that you met the training, experience, vision and examination requirements for a method and level.

Can I take the practical exam online?

No. The practical is performed with real equipment on real specimens. Simulators such as Practical NDT help you practise, but they are not a practical exam.

Can I get certified without an employer?

Under SNT-TC-1A, certification is issued by an employer. ASNT's central certifications (ASNT NDT Level II and Level III) are issued by ASNT, but the Level II still relies on the employer for the practical and vision exams, and all of them require documented experience.

Which NDT methods can be studied online?

Theory for all common methods (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET and advanced UT such as PAUT and TOFD) can be studied online. Radiography also needs radiation safety training and whatever licensing the state or NRC requires.

Can Level III be done online?

The preparation can be done entirely online, because the ASNT Level III Basic and method exams are written, computer-based exams taken at a test centre.

Is free online NDT certification real?

Free courses can teach useful theory, but no free website can certify you. Certification needs experience, a practical exam and an employer or ASNT behind it.

How does Atlantis handle the practical part?

We deliver hands-on training and administer the practical exam onsite at the employer's facility under an ASNT Level III, after trainees complete live online theory and simulator practice.

How do I start?

Tell us the method, level and whether you have an employer sponsor, and we will set out the route and a quote within one business day.
